payload.rationale: The threshold requires a single-decimal rounding of 0.5% or higher. Recent months have seen high volatility (0.9% in March, -0.4% in June, 0.4% in August). Core CPI was 0.3% in August, suggesting underlying inflation is steady around 0.3%. Hitting 0.5% would likely require a significant positive contribution from volatile components like energy or food. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that energy prices could fall or stabilize by October, keeping headline CPI closer to core at 0.2% or 0.3%. The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is that the recent trend of high volatility could continue, and a spike in gasoline or other commodities could easily push headline CPI to 0.5% or higher, as seen in earlier months of 2026.
limitations: October and November price data are not observed. No current commodity-price forecast or complete CPI component model is supplied.
PCE is a different index from CPI; annual inflation is not monthly inflation. Strict threshold and one-decimal rounding matter.
Small coordinator-selected packet; no fitted probability model or complete research review.
Different questions can share source information and economic drivers; do not treat their errors as independent.
